stories.headline: Jags' Travis Hunter to play both ways, but plan is fluid
stories.summary: Travis Hunter will play both ways for the Jaguars, but how much is still fluid.
stories.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said again that Travis Hunter is going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026.

But there's a chance that might not happen every week.

Coen said he doesn't feel like he must get Hunter offensive snaps each week and that the way each game unfolds will play a part in determining when -- or even if -- he plays at all on that side of the ball. There's no set plan.

"I don't," Coen said Friday as the Jaguars continued preparations for Sunday's season opener against Cleveland at EverBank Stadium. "I have a lot of confidence in Travis to go out and compete for us. He hasn't played a lot of football since he got hurt and it's really at the end of the day, this is about winning football games."

Hunter spent the majority training camp on defense and he will start at cornerback Sunday. Whatever offensive plan the Jaguars have for Hunter each week will be fluid, and it won't be a guarantee that Hunter touches the ball when he is on the field.

"You're going to continue to try to get him in positions that he can do things that he's good at," Coen said. "That's what we're trying to do. It doesn't always [mean Hunter is going to get the ball when he's in the game]. He's a damn good blocker. He can run routes in terms of maybe the ball's not schemed up to go to him.

"I'm not obviously having a count in my head with how many plays and what we're exactly going to do with him, but he definitely will play both."

Sunday will be Hunter's first game since he suffered a season-ending torn lateral collateral ligament in his right knee during an Oct. 30 practice. He had surgery on Nov. 11, rehabbed during the rest of the season, and participated in the team's offseason program on a limited basis. He was cleared fully for training camp.

Hunter had his best offensive performance as a rookie in his final game last season, catching eight passes for 104 yards and his first NFL touchdown during a 35-7 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 7.

The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner and second overall pick in 2025 ended his season with 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown and 15 tackles and three pass breakups. He played 67% of the team's offensive snaps and 36% of the defensive snaps until his injury.

stories.headline: Sources: Suns' Mark Williams to miss months after shoulder surgery
stories.summary: Phoenix Suns center Mark Williams had surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss several months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.body:
Phoenix Suns center Mark Williams had surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss several months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Williams, 24, who signed a fully guaranteed three-year, $38 million deal to return to the Suns in free agency, suffered the injury in an offseason workout recently.

He was coming off the healthiest season of his four-year NBA career, appearing in 60 games after a previous high of 44. He averaged 11.7 points, 8.0 rebounds and 0.9 blocks in 23.6 minutes per game.

Williams arrived in Phoenix in a 2025 draft night deal from Charlotte, after the Hornets' first attempt to trade him was rescinded shortly at that year's trade deadline. Williams took over as the Suns' starting center and was part of a group that helped Phoenix beat preseason expectations in earning a playoff berth.

He has career averages of 12 points, 8.5 rebounds and one block per game.

stories.headline: Fever's Sophie Cunningham not worried about off-court distractions
stories.summary: Sophie Cunningham said she's focusing on the Fever's remaining games and not the commotion around Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declaring for the WNBA draft.
stories.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said Friday that she's focusing on her team's four remaining regular-season games and not the commotion around Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declaring themselves eligible for the WNBA draft.

"I'm gonna let them do them," Cunningham told ESPN as part of a wide-ranging interview. "I'm just focused on the Fever and on our sport. I think we have four more games left. I'm trying to just really dial in and keep the main thing the main thing."

Kanter Freedom, who posted his intention to play in the WNBA on social media on Aug. 7, was ejected from the Fever's game against the Chicago Sky on Aug. 23 in Chicago following a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. He has since filed a lawsuit arguing his First Amendment rights had been violated.

White attended a Fever game against the Connecticut Sun on Aug. 28.

Cunningham said she supported restricting transgender girls and women from girls' and women's sports in an ESPN article published July 21.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that,'" Cunningham said in the article. "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

Rallies for and against transgender inclusion popped up at Fever games in the weeks after the article. The WNBA has been on a break since Aug. 31 while many of its stars, including the Fever's Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston, compete in the FIBA World Cup in Berlin.

The Fever, who return to the court next Friday in Toronto, are 26-14 and in fifth place in the standings. The team is battling for home-court advantage in the first round of the playoffs, which begin Sept. 27.

On Thursday, Cunningham, who is averaging 8.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists, relaunched her podcast with new host Drew Hanlen and with the new name "No Hesitation."

"I think this team has great potential to make a really great playoff run," Cunningham said. "And if I'm filling my brain and my energy with all that stuff, then it's taking away from the team. And so I'm just trying to stay here and let them do what they want to do."

stories.headline: Tottenham's Roberto De Zerbi says Mykhailo Mudryk suffered 'stupid' injury
stories.summary: Tottenham Hotspur boss Roberto De Zerbi has called new arrival Mykhailo Mudryk's injury "stupid" and has backed the winger to return to action soon.
stories.body:
Tottenham Hotspur boss Roberto De Zerbi has labelled new arrival Mykhailo Mudryk's injury as "stupid" and has backed the winger to return to action soon.

Chelsea loanee Mudryk made his first competitive appearance in 22 months in the 0-0 draw with Forest on Saturday after he served a suspension for recording an "adverse finding" of banned substance meldonium in 2024, but it will be followed by a lengthy spell out.

Sources told ESPN that the Ukraine international is set to be sidelined until October at the earliest after suffering an ankle injury in training.

"[With] Mudryk, it was a stupid injury and we hope he can come back as soon as possible. For him and for us," De Zerbi told a news conference on Friday.

"For him because he suffered too much and for us because we lost an important player.

"He played 15 minutes in Nottingham, he played well, but it's in the normal process when one player doesn't play for a long time."

Spurs remain without a goal or win in the Premier League after a summer of lavish spending and big changes, but De Zerbi is relaxed.

"I think we are better than last season, especially the end of the season, many, many injuries. It's difficult to believe right now because we are not winning, we are not scoring, but I'm positive," De Zerbi said.

"I believe in my players, I believe in this group of players. I think the players have big, big qualities, big potential, and now I'm positive."

stories.headline: Spanish Grand Prix: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli sets pace in second practice, George Russell fifth
stories.summary: George Russell was left trailing Kimi Antonelli in second practice for the Spanish Grand Prix -- as British rookie Arvid Lindblad crashed out at Formula 1's new "risky" and "car-killer" venue in Madrid.
stories.body:
George Russell was left trailing Kimi Antonelli in second practice for the Spanish Grand Prix -- as British rookie Arvid Lindblad crashed out at Formula 1's new "risky" and "car-killer" venue in Madrid.

Championship leader Antonelli saw off Charles Leclerc by 0.113 seconds, with the latter half a tenth clear of teammate Lewis Hamilton in the other Ferrari. Lindblad recorded the fourth best time, a place ahead of Russell, before he became the circuit's first big victim.

Lindblad, 19, lost control of his Racing Bulls through the long left-hander at Turn 13. He slammed into the barrier and sustained significant damage to his car.

"I am sorry, everyone," he said over the radio. "I am glad you are OK," replied his relieved race engineer, Pierre Hamelin.

Lindblad's accident arrived after a number of drivers expressed their fears that the Madring street circuit -- with its imposing concrete walls and high-speed corners -- would lead to a series of accidents.

Russell described it as the "riskiest" on the Formula 1 calendar and Max Verstappen, rightly it proved, predicted it would be a "car killer."

Russell's British media session inside Mercedes' hospitality suite on Friday morning coincided with Formula 2 driver Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak's car bursting into flames after the Thai crashed at Turn 19. Inthraphuvasak, 20, escaped without injury after leaping out of his burning car.

"Oh wow," said Russell as he watched the grisly scene unfold on the TV. "This circuit is mental.

"There is less margin here than Monaco. Purely because of the speed. In Monaco, the walls are closer but because you're going a lot slower, if you make a mistake, you're not into the wall as quickly. Here, there's less margin."

- Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc held face-to-face talks after Monza woes: 'It's healthy'

- Spanish Grand Prix: Everything you need to know about F1's brand-new Madring

- Spanish Grand Prix: George Russell tops first session around F1's brand-new track in Madrid

Russell was asked what bearing Inthraphuvasak's fiery accident has on his psyche as a driver.

"I don't think too much to be honest," he replied as fire marshals extinguished the flames on Inthraphuvasak's wrecked machine.

"I'm sure my mother worries more than I do when she sees any crash. But for me, I'm content with whatever happens. This is part of the risk. You can hurt yourself doing anything.

"I was playing with my three-year-old nephew, who was on a quad, and I was on an electric bike racing him through the garden.

"I was next to him, and he looked at me, and as he looked, he turned, and he's wiped me out. He's gone barrel-rolling on the quad. I've gone barrel-rolling on the electric bike. That was the one that hurt the most!"

Russell's world championship hopes were dealt a setback at the previous round in Monza a week ago after he saw Antonelli win from 19th on the grid in identical Mercedes machinery.

Here, he admitted that he now needs luck on his side to stop Antonelli from winning the championship. The Italian has won seven times so far, while Russell has just two victories.

Russell topped the first running but Antonelli's advantage later in the day -- 0.337 seconds -- could leave the Brit with a sinking feeling heading into the rest of the weekend on the sport's return to the Spanish capital after a 45-year hiatus.

stories.headline: Dylan Larkin to attend Red Wings camp despite trade request
stories.summary: Longtime captain Dylan Larkin will be at Red Wings training camp despite requesting a trade this offseason. Though Larkin will be in attendance, the team said it will begin the season without a captain.
stories.body:
Longtime Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin will report to training camp in Detroit next week despite his summer trade request.

However the Red Wings announced that they will begin the season without a captain.

"Over the past couple of weeks, Red Wings leadership and I have had several in-depth discussions. I've appreciated those candid conversations, and I will be at training camp with my teammates," Larkin said in a statement. "When new leadership is in place, we'll talk further about the direction of the team. We will keep those conversations private, and I will keep my focus on the season ahead and on the guys in that room."

In July, shortly after Larkin's trade request became public, the Red Wings announced that Steve Yzerman would no longer be the team's general manager. Yzerman, a franchise legend and Hall of Famer, had been GM since 2019. Detroit entered a rebuild in that time and hasn't made the playoffs in 10 years.

In a statement, the Red Wings said they "look forward to seeing Dylan and his teammates at Little Caesars for the start of training camp," which begins Sept. 17.

"Any further discussions or decisions regarding this topic will be made once new hockey operations leadership is in place," the team said.

The Red Wings have hired a search firm, which has been conducting interviews for a new general manager.

Larkin, 30, grew up in nearby Waterford, Michigan, and played at the University of Michigan. He was selected by his hometown team in the first round of the 2014 NHL draft.

He debuted in the 2015-16 season for the Red Wings, and the team made the playoffs in his rookie season -- the final year of the franchise's NHL-record 25-year playoff streak. Detroit lost to Tampa Bay in five games in the first round and hasn't returned since.

Larkin was a key member of the 2026 U.S. men's Olympic team that won its first gold medal since 1980. He was especially important defensively and on special teams, part of a penalty killing unit that went a flawless 18-for-18 in Milan.

The Minnesota Wild -- led by Bill Guerin, also the general manager of Team USA -- have tried to acquire Larkin, according to sources. However the sides have been at a stalemate this summer, especially as Detroit's GM seat is vacant.

Larkin had been Detroit's captain since 2021. He ranks 10th in franchise history in both goals (276) and points (643).

The Red Wings' offseason has been defined by uncertainty. That led in part to the free agent departure of Patrick Kane, who returned to the Chicago Blackhawks. Another key piece of business that's unresolved: ascending star defenseman Simon Edvinsson is due for a contract extension.

stories.headline: What We Learned: Knights never give up; Bennett's selections puzzled
stories.summary: The Newcastle Knights have beaten South Sydney at Allianz Stadium, advancing to the second week of the final. Here's what we learned from the game.
stories.body:
The Newcastle Knights have beaten South Sydney at Allianz Stadium, advancing to the second week of the finals, sending the Rabbitohs crashing out of what was a promising season.

Here are three things we learned from the game:

Knights never stop fighting

Suspensions, injuries, away from home - don't worry about any of it. Very few gave Newcastle a shot in this one but right from the jump they were more physical, more enthusiastic and took their chances. It wasn't a typical Knights showing because while they did score a long-range try, they had a mountain of ball in territory and won this via attrition rather than dazzling football.

Both first half tries came off kicks, but it was being in good attacking positions to end their sets which allowed that to happen. All week, a lot of people, including me, thought if they'd win it would be by throwing a few counter punches and defending gamely. They didn't really need to.

They were meant to be the team on the back foot, with a forward pack devoid of stars They dominated in yardage, robbed Souths of good ball, and suffocated their way to victory. It's so against type for them it's hard to really believe, but as hard-earned a win as the Knights have got all year. Bring on week two.

Bennett's selection puzzlers finally catch up

The loudest cheer from the Souths fans at the Sydney Football Stadium didn't come at kick off, or even when Campbell Graham scored - rather, it was Jye Gray being subbed on to the field in the second half that got the punters up and about.

Gray is beloved by Rabbitohs supporters and with good reason; he was one of the few bright sparks in an awful 2025 season and has made stuff happen every time he's on the field in 2026.

However, a few weeks' ago, coach Wayne Bennett made the decision to bench Gray in favour of Matt Dufty, who's return to the NRL after several years in the wilderness has been a great story in its own right - but it's a decision that's puzzled plenty, including me. Dufty was poor in kick defence for each of the opening two tries and threw a late intercept to stop any hopes of a comeback. It was a selection misfire.

Similarly, after Ashton Ward was ruled out for the season it was assumed that Jamie Humphreys would be the halfback the rest of the way. Instead it was Bud Sullivan who Bennett went with, and his decision making on Friday night was pretty rough for the most part.

Still, both Sullivan and Dufty have had great moments at times. The other and much more puzzling situation has been the refusal to play hooker Peter Mamouzelos, the most creative nine at the club and best foil to Brandon Smith. Every single Souths fan I've spoken to is baffled as to why Mamouzelos can't get into the team, particularly when the players who are getting minutes at hooker instead of him aren't hookers by trade. It makes no sense.

All of this is largely moot though because without Cody Walker, Souths weren't going to make any real impact on the finals series, even if they had stolen this one late on. Maybe next year.

Back-row brilliance from Newcastle

Take a bow, Jermaine McEwen and Francis Manuleleua. McEwen especially was superb with his two tries, but it was the edge integrity that allowed the Knights to stay on top in this one. Souths are so deadly on both sides but particularly their left, but for the most part those sweeping raids to the flanks were shut down with ease and that begins with the backrowers.

Again, this wasn't a position where you looked at Newcastle as having an advantage, but they were just better on the night.

We all know about the stars that the Knights have in other areas of the field, many of whom were great tonight. But if they can get this level of production from less-heralded guys, who knows how far they can go?

stories.headline: Sources: Patriots' A.J. Brown to go on IR, miss at least 4 games
stories.summary: The Patriots are placing wide receiver A.J .Brown on injured reserve due to his high ankle sprain, sidelining him for a minimum of four games, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.body:
The New England Patriots are placing wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve due to his high ankle sprain, sidelining him for a minimum of four games, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

An MRI confirmed Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Wednesday's season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks that is expected to sideline him for at least four weeks, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Thursday.

X-rays did not reveal a fracture.

The Patriots will be without Brown for the Sept. 20 home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers, then road games against the Jacksonville Jaguars (Sept. 27) and Buffalo Bills (Oct. 4). New England then has back-to-back home games against the Las Vegas Raiders (Oct. 11) and New York Jets (Oct. 18).

Brown had quickly emerged as quarterback Drake Maye's go-to target in the receiver's debut for the team.

Veteran Mack Hollins took over the majority of Brown's role Wednesday after he left the game early in the third quarter. The Patriots will also need more from former Green Bay Packer Romeo Doubs, who had a costly drop and finished without a catch in his Patriots debut after signing a four-year, $68 million free agent contract in the offseason.

Four-year veteran DeMario Douglas (slot) and second-year players Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III are also on the depth chart. Receiver was one of the team's deepest positions in training camp, leading to the trade of former starter Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans.

Brown remained down after a third-down incompletion in which Maye was throwing in his direction with Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett in tight coverage. Pritchett's right knee appeared to land on Brown's ankle with the force of his body weight. Brown grabbed for the back of his right leg as he sat up.

He slowly walked to the sideline, going to the medical tent for an extended period. He then walked to the locker room with members of the athletic training and medical staff.

The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles on June 1.

Earlier in the game, Brown helped set up the Patriots' first touchdown by coming back for an underthrown deep ball by Maye and drawing a defensive pass interference penalty. Maye hit rookie tight end Eli Raridon for a 2-yard touchdown on the next play.

Sept. 8: What history may tell us about Clippers' future + key signings in the West
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to cover the latest fallout from the LA Clippers' punishment after the NBA announced its punishments for the franchise's off-the-court dealings with Kawhi Leonard. They discuss what league history could tell us about what's ahead for the Clippers and how LA got into this situation. They then close on key deals in the West, including Ben Simmons signing with the Sacramento Kings and Amen Thompson's extension with the Houston Rockets.

Topics:

0:27: Updates on the fallout from Clippers' punishment

Windhorst on the league's reaction to the Clippers' punishment: "I think Steve Balmer had support of his peers in this, even though these was pretty severe accusations.

"I'm not saying everybody again, but I think people wanted to believe him, his peers. I'm not talking about the other GMs. I'm not talking about the agents. ...

"So the word that was said to me by a very influential person was that the other owners, some of the other owners were aghast when they read this report. That was the word that was used to me, aghast. And regardless of what Steve says, the support that he had is no longer there."

Windhorst on the Clippers' best course of action now: "When the Wolves were found guilty, Glen Taylor said words that were not, "I'm guilty." Kevin McHale, who was the vice president of basketball operations, said, 'I didn't even know this existed.' You know, he pled ignorance.

"[Then] They thought about it. They ended up negotiating with the league office and they pled guilty. And two days after basically they raised the white flag in December, David Stern gave him back a pick and a year later he gave him back the second pick. Now he gave them back -- he took away five years of picks [previously] -- he gave them back Year 3 at first and then Year 5. It wasn't like he gave him back immediately. But I think the Clippers should study that."

MacMahon on why Houston extended Thompson now: "I've been telling you for a while just how much the Rockets value Thompson. If there's one untradeable player on the roster, it is him.

"According to their metrics, they think he's one of the top 10 -- and I might be inflating that number -- most valuable players in the league. Now, we can argue and we can debate and you can say that's ridiculous. I'm just telling you the way that they view him. And so for them to get a player they value that much on this deal is great value for them.

"And for Amen Thompson, $208 million fully guaranteed and there's no options either way in the deal, he's set for life. He wants to be in Houston. He's going to be in Houston."

Sept. 3: EMERGENCY POD: NBA announces Clippers' punishments after Kawhi probe
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to react to the hefty punishments handed down to the LA Clippers by the NBA after the investigation into Kawhi Leonard's off-court dealings. They break down what this means for the future of the Clippers, if the punishment makes sense and if this will impact Leonard's pending trade to the Toronto Raptors.

Topics:

7:04 :The Clippers' argument against the NBA in this

MacMahon on why the penalty was so large for the Clippers: "The simple fact of the matter is this ain't the first time Steve Balmer's pulled this shady stuff. That did not help his case.

"They gave him a little slap on the wrist for the DeAndre Jordan stuff in 2015. $250,000 fine. It was 'Oh, whoops. We didn't know.' And then, there's the investigation for the Kawhi signing because, guess what? It's not like Uncle Dennis only asked the Clippers for a whole bunch of under-the-table stuff. He was asking everybody for under-the-table stuff. 'Oh, geez. You know, we were asked, but we didn't, you know, didn't give him anything' and and now this. So, in a way they're three-time losers."

Windhorst on the Clippers' best course of action following the ruling: "If they could get an agreement, if they could plead guilty, get an agreement and and say, 'We're not going to challenge any of these penalties.' And they get an agreement that there'll be no further penalties -- basically, they'll say that these five first-round picks are all-encompassing, they cover everything. It's a blanket agreement and [then] they keep their nose clean, and they do the Kawhi trade, they might be able to come out of this without four broken limbs. They may be able to come out of this with less damage."

MacMahon on one of the winners of the investigation: "I do think Adam Silver in a way is a winner of this because straight up, he had been soft on crime as the commissioner since, ironically, he booted the previous Clippers owner, which was completely different circumstances."

Slater on the potential Curry extension in Golden State and why he could wait: "One of the things in discussions I've been having with people is this idea of, let's say he's like, '[Taking less money for the team is] something I'd think about.' I would be surprised if he locked into a number now because, as you just saw with Draymond Green, the Warriors and their legendary figures are willing to trust each other in business.

"Draymond Green willingly gave up $27 million and went into unrestricted free agency where he couldn't have got $27 million back, [but] under the understanding if business didn't work out, he would get that money back. If you're Steph, you say, 'OK, you know what? I'll give y'all a crack at going and trying to find some stuff, but if you don't, at the end of the day, if I come back and say, give me the full max, I get the full max.'

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA and semifinal preview
stories.summary: The FIBA Women's World Cup semifinal matchups are set. How does each team stack up going into Saturday's games?
stories.body:
BERLIN -- The semifinals of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup are set, albeit with relatively few surprises.

The United State and France continued their undefeated runs with convincing wins over Hungary and China, respectively, in the quarterfinals. In the other games Thursday, Spain pounced on short-handed Australia, and host nation Germany -- playing in only its second World Cup -- upset reigning EuroBasket champ Belgium.

The host country has now made the semifinals in each of the past six World Cups, medaling in half those instances. Play will resume Saturday with the semifinals, followed by the medal rounds on Sunday.

The U.S. women are aiming for their fifth consecutive World Cup gold and 12th overall; the program has lost only one game at a major international tournament -- the World Cup and Olympics -- since 1994.

But the United States hasn't looked entirely invincible in this tournament -- it hasn't helped to be without A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum -- and it has never been more clear that the gap between the Americans and the rest of the world is rapidly closing.

Here's what you need to know about the last four teams standing. The number in parenthesis reflects the team's current FIBA ranking (last updated on April 1).

Germany (11) vs. France (2)

10:30 a.m. ET Saturday

Current Germany WNBA players:

F Frieda Buhner, Portland Fire

G Leonie Fiebich, New York Liberty

C Luisa Geiselsoder, Portland Fire

F Nyara Sabally, Toronto Tempo

Current France WNBA players:

G Pauline Astier, New York Liberty

F Valeriane Ayayi, Phoenix Mercury

G Marine Johannes, New York Liberty

G Leila Lacan, Connecticut Sun

G Carla Leite, Portland Fire

C Dominique Malonga, Seattle Storm

F Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

G Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries

How do they match up:

This will be a matchup of two teams with something to prove. After getting tantalizingly close to beating the U.S. for the gold at the 2024 Olympics, France has not shied from saying it's going for it all in Berlin.

"All we care about is winning," Malonga said after France beat China. "The French national team has been known for years for like second place or semifinals, never all the way, even in EuroBasket, until now -- I feel like we have to do it. We have to make it happen."

Players credited Golden State Valkyries star Williams for helping change the culture of the French national team to one of high standards, accountability and confidence. Players aren't just happy to be there, but instead want to win and make history as perhaps the greatest team to ever suit up for France.

France is certainly playing like a squad that could win gold, beating teams by an average of 39 points. Les Bleues are known for their defensive identity, but the group has shined offensively this World Cup, averaging 98.8 points on 53.3% shooting, including a blistering 45.7% from the 3-point arc.

Germany, meanwhile, is enjoying its best-ever finish in either of the two major international tournaments, all while being without star Satou Sabally and having to bounce back from a crushing 30-point rout to Spain to open the tournament.

In fact, Germany's quarterfinal upset over Belgium might already be the best day in the history of its women's team, multiple players said. Coach Olaf Lange said he was a little speechless with how well his team played, with six players scoring in double figures and stars Fiebich (17 points, 10 rebounds) and Nyara Sabally (16 points, 12 rebounds) finishing with double-doubles.

Thursday's result alone ensures the 2026 World Cup is a success for Germany, but it has more to compete for. Multiple players were asked about the game being a rematch of the quarterfinals from the Paris Olympics -- a 84-71 France victory -- and the pain of that loss was clearly still fresh even two years later.

The Germans once more will be considered the underdogs against France but will receive a major boost from their fans, who have filled Uber Arena in droves throughout the tournament, as they look to keep making history on home soil.

United States (1) vs. Spain (6)
2 p.m. ET Saturday

Current USA WNBA players:

F/C Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever

G Paige Bueckers, Dallas Wings

G Sonia Citron, Washington Mystics

G Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever

F Napheesa Collier, Minnesota Lynx

F/G Kahleah Copper, Phoenix Mercury

G Chelsea Gray, Las Vegas Aces

G Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream

F Kiki Iriafen, Washington Mystics

F Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream

F Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty

G Jackie Young, Las Vegas Aces

Current Spain WNBA players:

G Elena Buenavida, Minnesota Lynx (developmental player)

C Raquel Carrera, New York Liberty

F Maria Conde, Toronto Tempo

C Megan DiLeo, Portland Fire

C Awa Fam, Seattle Storm

G Alicia Florez, Washington Mystics

How do they match up:

On Thursday, the U.S. took another step toward making its group phase scare against Italy look like an anomaly, demolishing Hungary by 52 points and setting or flirting with a litany of records.

One positive development from the quarterfinal was the way Collier came out aggressive and productive from the jump, scoring 10 first-quarter points and 19 on the game -- notably, that's her senior team personal best in scoring (besting the 12 points she scored Monday against Czechia).

The Lynx star is still working her way back from a long rehab process following double ankle surgery this offseason, but the more she plays the way she has in the past two games, the better for the Americans. She and Young -- the only U.S. player to reach double figures each game -- are now the top scorers for the Americans this tournament.

"I think just moving a lot without the ball," Collier said of how she found success Thursday. "Making sure I'm super active, getting second-chance opportunities, cutting, just playing my normal game a little bit more."

Across the board, the team felt this was its best performance of the World Cup, not only because of what it accomplished offensively but because of how it started on defense. There was also a recognition that now, 10 or so days into the tournament, the chemistry is starting to come together and players are learning how to play alongside each other even more.

All of that bodes well going into the final two days of games. That said, neither Hungary nor Czechia were the toughest of tests for the U.S. Spain -- which nearly took home EuroBasket gold the past two tournaments -- should be much stiffer competition. If over the weekend things get mucked up offensively, or the U.S. finds itself struggling more generally, all eyes will be on how the team learned from the Italy experience in how to work through adversity, both in which individuals step up and how the group comes together.

Spain, which features a litany of current and former WNBA players, had a perplexing loss to Mali on the second day of its group phase, but it features an intriguing mix of experienced vets and young talent that've propelled it back to within reach of a fourth medal in the past five World Cups.

The unit took down Australia with a well-rounded effort that included six players scoring at least nine points. But to knock off the Americans, it feels as if Spain will need to have breakout games from its 20-year-old pair of Iyana Martin and Fam, the former a Portland Fire first-round draft pick and the latter a Seattle Storm rookie.

stories.headline: Monaco's Lamine Camara says he has 'turned the page' after failed Chelsea move
stories.summary: Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara said he has moved on from his collapsed move to Chelsea and is fully focused on playing well for the Ligue 1 leaders.
stories.body:
Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara said he has moved on from his collapsed move to Chelsea and is fully focused on playing well for the Ligue 1 leaders.

When it first appeared that United States forward Folarin Balogun's move to Premier League side Everton was off, Monaco negotiated with Chelsea over selling Camara amid a chaotic end to the summer transfer window.

The clubs reached an agreement with just hours left in the window, Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro said. But the deal was suddenly scrapped when Everton reversed their decision on Balogun and attempted to get that signing done. In the end, neither player moved and both are still at the French club.

"There was a possibility I could leave. It didn't go through at the last minute and that's part of football," Camara said on Friday ahead of Monaco's game at Strasbourg on Saturday. "I've turned the page and am focusing on the season."

Monaco were under pressure to transfer Balogun or another top player like Camara to comply with the French league's financial rules. But Camara says he hasn't let the situation affect him.

"It's part of a professional player's life. I managed to stay professional and not dwell on it too much," he said. "Once it's happened there's no point in thinking about it again."

Camara was a standout for Monaco last season and the 22-year-old, who is a regular for Senegal, is very highly rated by new Monaco coach Filipe Luís.

- Chelsea under Xabi Alonso are unlike anything the Premier League has seen before

- Xabi Alonso enjoys Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer's man of the match argument

- Hull's Sergej Jakirovic jokes about plan to stop Chelsea: 'Kick them'

Camara did well in last Friday's 2-1 win at defending champions Paris Saint-Germain and said he knows another strong season will logically lead to more offers from big clubs.

"I can help the team a lot," he said. "Football moves fast, maybe other opportunities will come along. But for now, I'm staying focused on the season with Monaco."

stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli topped the times in the second practice session of the Spanish Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Title leader Kimi Antonelli topped the times in the second practice session at the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.

He beat Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari to the line by 0.113 seconds, with Lewis Hamilton in third.

Re-live Friday's practice sessions below.

- Spanish Grand Prix: Everything you need to know about F1's brand-new Madring

- Spanish Grand Prix: George Russell tops first session around F1's brand-new track in Madrid

The Madring is a hybrid between a street circuit and a purpose-built track, using a mixture of public roads and private land around the IFEMA Madrid exhibition centre.

The circuit is 5.416km long and features 22 corners. Sunday's race will take place over 57 laps.

Formula 1 is returning to Madrid for the first time since 1981, when the Spanish Grand Prix was held at Jarama, around 30 kilometres north of the city.

Mercedes' George Russell said ahead of the weekend: "I would put it, arguably, as the most risky circuit of the whole calendar, because you have real high-speed corners, sort of Jeddah-esque. The walls are very close. There's no margin for error.

"But then, you have other corners that are quite like Baku, where you're coming from a high speed into a slow braking zone. You're braking and turning at the same time.

"So, locking tyres is going to be easy. If you're not coping, you'll be straight in the wall.

"I think it's going to be really challenging for us as drivers. The race is going to be challenging to overtake. So, on the whole, it's not an easy one."

Alpine's Pierre Gasly added: "I must say it's exciting, but at the same time I think it's going to be quite a disruptive weekend, how easy it will be to have a crash."

stories.headline: Fenerbahçe coach Kartal misses training despite club blocking resignation
stories.summary: Fenerbahçe coach Ismail Kartal announced his shock resignation after the 1-1 draw against Roma, but club president Aziz Yildirim said the coach remains in his position.
stories.body:
Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal failed to appear at training on Friday, Turkish media reports said, a day after he announced he was stepping down following a draw against Roma in a Champions League game but the club refused to accept his resignation.

Kartal stunned a postmatch news conference following the 1-1 draw against Roma by announcing his intention to leave the club, a move that club president Aziz Yıldırım swiftly rejected.

"I have stepped down tonight," Kartal said. "I made this decision to clear the way for my club. I am resigning with the intention of never returning."

Kartal, who returned to the Istanbul side in June 2026 for his fourth stint, thanked the club for its support and congratulated his players on a match "we could have won," before adding that "from now on, to help Fenerbahçe, my footballers, I have resigned from my position, on the condition of never returning."

The announcement caught club officials entirely off guard, prompting Yıldırım to address the media minutes later to override the manager's decision.

"İsmail Kartal remains in charge. The club must support our coach. As long as I remain president, Kartal is the Fenerbahçe coach," Yıldırım said.

"There is no need for İsmail Kartal to say he will continue. I am his superior; I tell him, 'You will continue,' and that's that."

Playing in front of a sold-out Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium, Fenerbahçe marked their return to Europe's top-tier competition for the first time since the 2008-09 campaign.

Roma opened the scoring when Bryan Cristante capitalized with a low shot from outside the box in the 39th minute. Fenerbahçe responded early in the second half when left back Archie Brown expertly flicked the ball over the goalkeeper to equalize in the 48th minute.

Fenerbahçe will return to action on Monday to face Gaziantep FK in the Turkish Super Lig.

Information from the Associated Press contributed to this report.

Sept. 11: Friday's Forecaster findings
By Tristan H. Cockcroft

Over the next 10 days of play, we're almost certain to see our first significant postseason berths clinched. The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers are virtual locks to assure themselves playoff berths (as a starting point) during the Sept. 11-13 weekend and several teams are within reach of celebrating during the upcoming week.

The Brewers (magic number of 5) and Los Angeles Dodgers (6) can clinch their respective divisions, and the New York Yankees (4), Dodgers (5), Atlanta Braves (8) and Boston Red Sox (9) can clinch wild-card spots, all of which seem likely to occur during fantasy's Week 24. From a player motivation standpoint, fantasy managers should prefer players from games with something on the line, and it's not uncommon for a team clinching some type of postseason berth or seeding to rest veteran players afterward, often in the game immediately following that happening.
The AL Central-leading Chicago White Sox visit the Cleveland Guardians, 1.5 games back in the division, for three games at Progressive Field from Monday through Wednesday.
The Toronto Blue Jays and Texas Rangers -- 1 and 2 games back in the AL wild-card race, respectively -- play three games at Globe Life Field from Friday through Sunday.
The Arizona Diamondbacks, 0.5 games back in the NL wild-card race, visit the Yankees, 3 games back in the AL East, from Friday through Sunday.
Fantasy managers could get boosts with the prospective returns of two injured hitters: Willson Contreras (hamstring) is on a minor league rehab stint and seems likely to be activated either at the start of or in advance of Boston's Week 24 road trip to Texas and Tampa Bay. Shea Langeliers (knee), once believed to be done for the season, is instead now on a minor league rehab stint and might begin to see some work as DH for the Athletics at some point during Week 24.
The Colorado Rockies play the entire week at Coors Field in one of only two weeks all season where they're scheduled for seven games there, and one of just four weeks played entirely at Coors. The Rockies do face a pair of talented pitching staffs in the San Diego Padres (4 games, Monday through Thursday) and Seattle Mariners (3, Friday through Sunday), but Coors' hitter-friendly confines nevertheless tilt things in favor of Rockies hitters in those matchups. Additionally, visiting Padres and Mariners hitters get to capitalize against Rockies pitching, which has baseball's worst ERA (5.50).

Brandon Marsh exited Thursday afternoon's game after fouling a ball off his foot in the eighth inning. The Philadelphia Phillies open an important road series with the Atlanta Braves tonight and Marsh's status is uncertain. The Phillies are four games behind the Braves for the NL East lead.

To replace Ohtani, the Dodgers are calling up Josue De Paula from Double-A Tulsa, who will join the team for Friday's matchup with the Miami Marlins. stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Sept. 10

Hogan set to join Pies

GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 35
Goals: 31
Assists: 14

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Song Yadong rises in divisional rankings after shocking KO
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Song Yadong scored the biggest victory of his career on Saturday at UFC Fight Night in Shanghai, knocking out onetime men's bantamweight title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov. The stunning second-round finish as a nearly 5-1 underdog propelled Song up three spots into the top four in the ESPN divisional rankings.

Nurmagomedov, who previously owned the No. 4 position at 135-pounds, slips down one spot, as do the other two fighters who had been ranked ahead of Song, Mario Bautista and Cory Sandhagen.

That was this week's only movement in the divisional rankings.

stories.headline: Knights break away finals curse, knock Bunnies out
stories.summary: Newcastle have killed South Sydney's premiership ambitions, knocking the Bunnies out in a 20-10 NRL finals win.
stories.body:
Newcastle are daring to dream of a deep finals run after pulling off a heist and dumping South Sydney out of the competition in a surprise 20-10 elimination final win.

On a night young back-rower Jermaine McEwen made everyone sit up and take notice with a two-try display at Allianz Stadium, the undermanned Knights advanced to next week's semi-final by upstaging Souths on their home patch.

The Knights will face the loser of Saturday's qualification between the Warriors and the Dolphins, after claiming their first finals win on the road since 2013.

Without five-eighth Dylan Brown and their first-choice front-row pairing of Trey Mooney and Daniel Saifiti, there would have been few pundits who would have given Newcastle a chance before kick-off on Friday.

But, inspired by Dane Gagai's running battle with South Sydney's Latrell Mitchell, last year's wooden spooners kept their premiership ambitions alive in front of a 28,152 crowd that included a healthy contingent of Novocastrians.

"I think the belief and confidence that coach (Justin Holbrook) instills in us, we don't worry about what we don't have," said Newcastle captain Kalyn Ponga.

"To have them (Newcastle fans) here impacting our performance is pretty special ... obviously we made them proud tonight and have all year but we have a few more to go."

On the other hand, next to nothing went right for the Bunnies in their first finals game since 2023.

Alex Johnston (groin) and Cody Walker (calf) trudged off with injuries, while Mitchell was largely kept quiet by Gagai who formed part of a fruitful right edge that was the Knights' main source of attack.

McEwen drew first blood down that side when he caught a Dom Young bat-back and raced in from 30m out to score a sixth minute opener.

Mitchell and Gagai's skirmish boiled over soon afterwards but when neither player landed a clean blow, referee Ashley Klein allowed both to stay on the field.

"It was a great battle and was always going to be so, but Gags was tremendous for us and did a really good job," Holbrook said.

The fracas injected some venom into a game in which the Knights slowly began to take the upper hand.

McEwen and fellow edge Francis Manuleleua made their presence felt on the Bunnies' edges before Gagai raced past Mitchell to dot down on a Sandon Smith grubber.

Rabbitohs winger Campbell Graham crashed over Greg Marzhew to get his side on the board as they trailed 10-6 at the break.

Souths struggled to connect after Walker limped off late in the second half and their only moment of magic came when Mitchell set the wheels in motion for a Jayden Sullivan try.

The Sullivan try was chalked off after a lengthy bunker review during which Johnston was adjudged to have knocked on.

"I'm over the decisions they make and the impact it has on teams," Souths coach Wayne Bennett said.

"I'd rather have the referee if he is doing his job properly, best he can. He'll make a mistake and I can live with that.

"What I can't live with is this thing called the bunker that's supposed to be 100 per cent perfect. It's not perfect."

Young helped swing the result in Newcastle's favour by making a break down the right to set up McEwen for his second try in the 62nd minute.

Four minutes later, the big English winger tip-toed down the sideline to score and all but send Holbrook's men into week two of the finals.

Jye Gray scored a late try but the Bunnies had left their run too late.
